title: Stored x-only leaf birthday search on secp256k1 at 125.567689: bulk-synchronous transport, every per-record kernel step executed and charged, port in-flight counts charged

claims.statement: For uniform production secp256k1 Q=[x]P, the classical cold stored-leaf birthday search of proof.md recovers x with probability at least 0.3900001 over the challenge and fresh algorithm coins, with no heuristic: the Chen-Stein method on cross-node leaf pairs bounds P(no collision), and drops, caps and the enumerated inline-carry sites of the kernels (section 3.4) are charged failure rows, while RNDR, the ideal coin source, adds none (section 6). On every run its total work is at most 2^125.567689 target-group-operation equivalents (1000 AArch64 instructions per unit). Machine (section 2.1): 2^72 nodes, each with one processor and a memory below 2^64 bytes, whose links only write a message's four words at the address its sender stored and report the write back to the port, with no flags, rings or counters; each port's in-flight count, which DSB waits on, is charged as 2 instruction-equivalents per message. Hop 1, hop 2 and grouping are charged 14.5, 16 and 30 per record (executed 12.5, 14 and 30, plus the in-flight counts); certificate.py gives 456.4082 instructions per leaf and the claim 125.567689. Peak memory 2^135.9988 bytes; preprocessing 2^111.0353 units, included; no advice. The bound is for the machine of section 2.1. Lineage: package 8f733826 (field rows, fe_inv, class row, a64.py); no prior acceptance or score is a premise. This is an analytic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Run the leaf kernels on production points, and the emit, both hops and the grouping on a 4 x 4 machine, against exact references; check the arithmetic sites of section 3.4; compare every kernel count with certificate.py; run the q25 toy and certificate.py. Budget-limited parts run stated minimums. Not a production-scale attack.
